title: Town Hall Tour Organizing Zoom - Eastern Idaho (6/17)
description:
Please join us for an organizing zoom call ahead of our third town hall leg in Eastern Idaho. On June 17th, we’ll be meeting at 5:30pm to discuss the logistics of pulling off a successful round of town halls to help inform the public of the dangers of vouchers and the need for people to get involved in this important fight.

During the 2025 legislative session, Idaho lawmakers passed House Bill 93 and enacted a $50 million school-voucher program. For the first time in state history, Idaho tax dollars will be used to subsidize the cost of tuition for private-school families. 

The special-interest groups promoting vouchers have made clear that the $50 million program is only the beginning. During next year’s legislative session, they intend to remove the $50-million cap and expand the program to all private-school families, including the wealthy, at an estimated cost of $339 million per year.
 
Such a massive expansion of vouchers would bankrupt Idaho and drain millions from public schools. For the benefit of a small number of private-school families, it would defund the public education system that serves 94% of Idaho’s kids. 

It may be inevitable that the legislature tries to expand House Bill 93, but it is not inevitable that they will succeed. To stop this attack on public schools, we need to get organized. Please sign up if you can make it and we hope to see you soon!

title: Stand Down for Veterans and Civilians Resource Event - Unite for Veterans, Unite for America
description:
This D-Day, Join us at Halifax Mall in Raleigh, NC, from 4-7 PM for a Stand Down for Veterans & Civilians Resource Event.

Join the 50501 Veterans, 50501NC, and our Veteran and civilian coalition partners as we partake in what is expected to be the largest nationwide coordination of veteran protests in the history of our country to support the rights and benefits Veterans earned through their service and sacrifice. We will have community resources, veteran organizations, and a food drive to benefit local Vets, courtesy of our IFNC allies.

This D-Day, the 2025 Bonus Army will march again, peacefully, across our nation. Join Us.

➡️Our Reasons Why
1. Reverse cuts to the VA, Rehire Fired Employees, & Fully Fund the PACT Act.
2. Ensure VA Support, Healthcare, & Counseling for MST Survivors.
3. Overturn the Trans Ban and Ensure full healthcare access for Trans Veterans and Active Duty Members.
4. Restore Protections for Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility (DEIA) in the VA and DoD. 
5. Protect Democracy, Restore Diplomatic Norms, and Maintain Strong Alliances with Global Democratic Leadership.
6. Return unjustly deported immigrant Veterans, and pass the Veteran Service Recognition Act & the Strengthening Citizenship Services for Veterans Act.

➡️Why June 6th, 2025 (80th Anniversary of D-Day)?
Our event is part of Unite for Veterans, Unite for America - a nationwide mass mobilization of several veteran and ally organizations. This is expected to be the largest coordinated nationwide Veterans' protest in the history of our country. The mobilization is modeled on the Bonus Army protests of tens of thousands of World War I Veterans in the summer of 1932 who peacefully descended with their families on Washington, D.C. Those Veterans had one simple demand - that America honor the promise made to them for their wartime service. At the height of the Great Depression, their promised bonuses were slashed by budget cuts. Facing hunger, homelessness, and despair, the Bonus Army rallied, determined to fight for the dignity they had earned on the battlefield. 

➡️What is a Stand Down Event? 
In times of war, exhausted combat units requiring time to rest and recover were removed from the battlefields to a place of relative security and safety. At secure base camp areas, troops were able to take care of personal hygiene, get clean uniforms, enjoy warm meals, receive medical and dental care, mail and receive letters, and enjoy the camaraderie of friends in a safe environment. Today, Stand Down refers to a grassroots, community-based intervention program designed to help the nation's estimated 107,000 homeless Veterans on any given night "combat" life on the streets. Homeless Veterans are brought together in a single location for one to three days and are provided access to the community resources needed to begin addressing their individual problems and rebuilding their lives. In the military, Stand Down afforded battle-weary soldiers the opportunity to renew their spirit, health, and overall sense of well-being. Today's Stand Down affords the same opportunity to homeless Veterans.

➡️What Should I Bring for the Food Drive? 
Please bring non-perishables to the event so that they can be donated to our local food banks that serve Veterans.

title: Estate Planning 101 with Attorney Jacquelyne J. Mingle
description:
Most people know that having a Will is important. Still, many still don’t have one. But get this: Having just a Will is not enough! Without crucial documents, people are leaving themselves and their estates vulnerable. Join the Sky Island Alliance and Tucson attorney Jacquelyne J. Mingle to learn estate planning basics and a little bit more.  This free public event is brought to you by [Sky Island Alliance](https://skyislandalliance.org/), [the Planned Giving Roundtable of Southern Arizona](https://www.pgrtsa.org/), and [Mission Management & Trust Co](https://missiontrust.com/). 

Attorney Jacquelyne J. Mingle: Jacque has been practicing in Tucson for more than a decade, and her practice encompasses a variety of elder law issues, including estate planning; estate and trust administration; and disputes over wills, trusts, and estates. She is a Fellow of the American College of Trust and Estate Counsel, is one of U.S. News & World Report’s “Best Lawyers,” and is a Certified by the State Bar of Arizona as a Specialist in Estate and Trust Law. She is licensed as a fiduciary by the Arizona Supreme Court and served as chair of the State Bar’s Elder Law, Mental Health and Special Needs Planning Council and served on the Estate & Trust Law Advisory Commission for the State Bar’s Board of Legal Specialization. She also serves on the Boards of Directors for the Southern Arizona Estate Planning Council and Tohono Chul Park. Jacque’s J.D. is from the U of A’s James E. Rogers College of Law, where she has taught the Trusts & Estates course as an adjunct professor. Before becoming an attorney, Jacque was an editor at USA Today supervising entertainment coverage. She did her undergraduate work at the University of Kansas and roots for both the Jayhawks (Rock Chalk!) and the Wildcats (Bear Down!).

Do you ever feel like your voice gets lost in the noise when it comes to important local issues like rising property taxes, public education funding, or emergency services? description:
If you haven't heard of it, On Tyranny: Twenty Lessons from the Twentieth Century is a book published in 2017 by Timothy Snyder, a historian of 20th-century Europe. ([Here is one appearance earlier this year](https://youtu.be/nNrbInmlHhA?si=pYLTz0pyAdK8nD31)). This book is more relevant than ever. Many of the warnings in the book are unfolding before our eyes right now. So, it's crucial to know how to recognize these signs, and more importantly, what we can learn from history and do differently this time.

The book is fairly short, only 126 pages, and would take just 2-3 hours to finish. If you need to purchase a copy, consider buying from a local bookstore.
